oneLiner: The time-to-power trade in its purest form: fuel cells for AI data centers drove revenue up 166%, a genuine profitability inflection, and gigawatt-scale frameworks with Oracle and AEP -- priced at ~17x forward sales, so conversion cadence is everything.
thesis: AI data centers turned fuel cells into baseload infrastructure. AEP finalized a 20-year offtake reported at $2.65B for up to 1 GW in January 2026, anchored by a ~900 MW Wyoming data-center campus (deal terms per press reports). Oracle followed on Apr 14, 2026 with a master agreement for up to 2.8 GW, with an initial 1.2 GW already contracted and Project Jupiter in New Mexico underway.

The profitability inflection arrived in Q2 2026. GAAP operating income swung to $182.2M on 33.4% gross margin (reported Jul 28, 2026), operating cash flow turned positive at $226.4M, and FY26 guidance implies $800-900M of non-GAAP operating income.

Capacity is the constraint, and it doubles this year. Fremont is expanding from a 1 GW to 2 GW annual run-rate by end-2026 (~$100M, on schedule as of Jul 2026) with the site expandable toward 5 GW; $2.69B of cash after the late-2025 convertible raise funds the buildout.

Brookfield removes the customer's capex barrier. The financing framework for Bloom-powered AI infrastructure was expanded fivefold from $5B to $25B on Jul 1, 2026, letting customers buy power-as-a-service instead of owning the equipment.

Hydrogen is a free option. Bloom's solid oxide platform runs in reverse as an electrolyzer (SOEC); revenue is negligible today, but it is the same factory and stack if green hydrogen economics ever arrive.

latestProse: Q2 2026 was Bloom's first billion-dollar quarter: revenue of $1,065.4M rose 165.5% on product revenue up 215%, GAAP gross margin hit 33.4%, and operating income swung to $182.2M from a small loss. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.78 versus $0.10 a year ago; adjusted EBITDA reached $253.4M versus $41.2M. Operating cash flow turned positive at $226.4M against a $213.1M burn in Q2 2025, leaving $2.69B of cash against $2.47B of recourse debt, and management raised full-year guidance for the second time this year. The disclosure that matters most: deferred revenue and customer deposits jumped to $327M from $101M at year-end 2025 -- AI data-center customers are now prepaying Bloom, funding its own working capital while it doubles manufacturing capacity.
guidanceProse: FY2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $3.9-4.2B (from $3.4-3.8B in April; roughly 100% growth over 2025's ~$2.0B), non-GAAP gross margin of about 34%, non-GAAP operating income of $800-900M, and non-GAAP EPS of $2.55-2.85. The constraint is capacity, not demand: the Fremont line doubles to 2 GW by year-end and management says the expansion is on schedule and on budget. Watch conversion of the Oracle (up to 2.8 GW) and AEP (up to 1 GW) frameworks into firm orders -- guidance assumes execution, not new mega-deals.
segments: Product: fuel-cell Energy Servers -- $935.4M in Q2 2026 (~88% of revenue, +215% YoY), sold to data centers, utilities, and C&I customers.
Service, installation, and electricity: recurring O&M on the installed base plus electricity sales; service profitability has historically lagged product and is the margin swing factor.
Electrolyzer (SOEC): high-efficiency solid oxide units sharing the fuel-cell platform; negligible revenue today, pure optionality on green hydrogen.
competitive: PLUG (PEM fuel cells, hydrogen): deeply unprofitable with its DOE loan support terminated; a cautionary comp on hydrogen economics, not a real competitor for data-center baseload.
FCEL: subscale, restructuring, no meaningful data-center traction; Bloom is the only SOFC maker operating at gigawatt scale.
GEV is the real competitor: gas turbines are cheaper per MW at scale, but slots are effectively sold out into 2028-29 -- Bloom sells time-to-power in months, not years.
Bridge power from recip engines (Caterpillar, Cummins) and, longer term, faster grid interconnection and SMRs compete for the same load.
On ~17x forward sales Bloom is priced like a tech platform; GEV trades far cheaper on sales, while PLUG and FCEL are option-value stocks (multiples approximate, Aug 2026).
moat: A decade of solid-oxide manufacturing learning gives Bloom the only at-scale SOFC platform, and 30-plus-point gross margins suggest real cost-curve advantage. But there is no patent wall against turbines, engines, or an eventually faster grid -- the moat today is time-to-power and a bankable delivery record. If interconnection queues shorten and turbine capacity catches up by 2028, the pricing premium erodes.
risks: Valuation: ~$70B market cap is ~17x FY26 guided revenue and ~75x forward non-GAAP EPS; the stock swung 11%+ on earnings day alone, so any growth wobble gets amplified.
'Up to' is not backlog: Oracle (2.8 GW) and AEP (1 GW) are frameworks; only ~1.2 GW of the Oracle MSA was contracted as of Apr 2026. Conversion cadence is the whole story.
Competition normalizes: GEV turbine capacity expands and interconnection queues shorten toward 2028-29, eroding the time-to-power premium that justifies Bloom's pricing.
Natural gas dependence: Energy Servers run predominantly on natural gas; sustained gas price spikes or adverse carbon rules dent both economics and the clean-power narrative.
Execution and concentration: doubling Fremont capacity while doubling revenue; related-party (SK ecoplant) revenue was $373.3M in Q1 2026 -- a lumpy channel.
Policy: tax-credit and tariff shifts remain swing factors for customer economics; the FY26 EPS guide leans on a favorable credit backdrop.
catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings (~late Oct 2026): Oracle MSA conversion and whether ~34% gross margin holds at higher volume.
Fremont 2 GW expansion completion by end-2026 (on schedule and on budget as of Jul 2026).
Oracle Project Jupiter (New Mexico) deployments and further tranches under the 2.8 GW MSA through 2027.
Brookfield $25B framework: first funded project announcements expected H2 2026.
AEP follow-on orders beyond the initial ~1 GW agreement; any new hyperscaler framework.
pricedIn: At roughly $210 and a ~$70B market cap (early Aug 2026), Bloom trades near 17x FY2026 guided revenue and roughly 75-80x the $2.70 midpoint of FY2026 non-GAAP EPS. That embeds years of hypergrowth: full conversion of the Oracle and AEP frameworks, capacity scaling past 2 GW toward Fremont's 5 GW potential, and mid-30s gross margins holding as volume doubles. What is not priced: hydrogen electrolyzer revenue (essentially zero today) and the Brookfield $25B framework converting into a repeatable annuity. What is priced and fragile: the assumption that gas turbines stay sold out and grid queues stay long through 2028 -- the entire premium rests on scarcity of alternatives.

scenarios.bear: AI capex digests in 2027; GEV and the turbine supply chain add capacity, interconnects speed up, and bridge-power premiums compress. Oracle and AEP take far less than the 'up to' volumes, growth decelerates to 20-30% off a $4B base, and gross margin slips below 30% on pricing pressure. At 30-40x a lower EPS path the stock retraces toward $60-90 -- still a good company, but a brutal de-rating from 17x sales.
scenarios.base: FY2026 lands near the $4.05B midpoint with ~34% gross margin and non-GAAP EPS of $2.55-2.85; the 2 GW Fremont expansion completes on schedule and 2027 revenue grows 30-45% as Oracle's initial 1.2 GW deploys and AEP follow-ons land. Margins hold as scale offsets pricing. The stock compounds with earnings rather than re-rating -- call it $200-260 -- with violent swings around each deal headline and quarter.
scenarios.bull: Time-to-power stays the binding constraint through 2028. Oracle converts most of its 2.8 GW, AEP expands beyond 1 GW, another hyperscaler signs, and Brookfield's $25B framework becomes a repeatable power-as-a-service engine. Capacity heads toward 3-5 GW, 2027-28 revenue compounds 50%+, EPS approaches $5 by 2028, and hydrogen SOEC adds a second act. Growth multiples hold and the stock pushes past $300.

valPresets.note: TTM FCF is unrepresentative: Q2 2026 was the first strongly positive OCF quarter (+$226M) and capex is elevated while Fremont doubles to 2 GW, so the DCF anchors on forward non-GAAP EPS (FY26 guide $2.55-2.85). Year-1 growth fades to 3% terminal: bear 8%, base 20%, bull 32%, tracking the scenario revenue paths.
